facts.name: PJM Rhododendron
facts.light: Full sun to part shade; keep it out of hot afternoon sun and wind
facts.moisture: Evenly moist, well drained; never soggy
facts.notes: One of the hardiest rhododendrons: an evergreen that covers itself in lavender-pink flowers in mid spring, and its small leaves turn deep purple for fall and winter. It has shallow roots, so keep it mulched and watered in dry spells, and water again in late fall before the ground freezes.
facts.soilWarn: Needs acidic soil (about pH 4.5 to 5.5). In soil that isn't acidic enough the leaves turn yellow. Get an MSU home soil test before planting; to lower pH, use sulfur or iron sulfate and mix in organic matter like pine needles or pine bark.
facts.toxSrc: ASPCA lists rhododendron as toxic to dogs, cats and horses; a few leaves can cause serious problems

sources.title: English Gardens (Metro Detroit garden centers): P.J.M. Rhododendron
sources.note: Sold at English Gardens: about 5 ft tall and wide, hardy to zone 3b; must have well-drained, acidic, organic soil; prune only after flowering.

prune.short: Right after it blooms: prune only if needed
prune.text: Prune only right after the flowers fade (late May into June), and never after July: next year's flower buds form over the summer, so later cuts remove them. It rarely needs pruning; to keep it about 4 to 5 ft, shorten a few long branches then and snap off the faded flower clusters if you like.

sources.title: English Gardens (Metro Detroit garden centers): P.J.M. Rhododendron
sources.note: About 5 ft tall and wide; full sun to part shade, away from hot afternoon sun; evenly moist, well-drained, rich acidic soil, yellow leaves (chlorosis) in alkaline soil; prune only after flowering; mulch the roots in winter in exposed spots.

sources.title: MSU Turfgrass archive: Rhododendrons flourish with companion plantings in acid soil (Dow Gardens, Midland, MI)
sources.note: PJM is the best-known, most adaptable hybrid of Carolina rhododendron, outstanding across the Midwest. Keep soil pH 4.5 to 5.5; lower it with sulfur or iron sulfate and add organic matter such as pine needles or pine bark for the shallow roots.

sources.title: Ask Extension (Wayne County, Michigan): rhododendron pruning and yellow leaves
sources.note: Prune just after it flowers. Yellow leaves can mean soil pH is too high; rhododendrons like pH 4.5 to 6.0. Get an MSU home soil test (homesoiltest.msu.edu) before adjusting.

sources.title: The Morton Arboretum: P.J.M. rhododendron
sources.note: 3 to 6 ft; one of the hardier rhododendrons and tolerates near-neutral soil. Shallow roots like mulch and water in dry spells. Avoid pruning after July, when next year's buds form.

sources.title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance (page 26)
sources.note: Rhododendrons (Rhododendron sp.) are rated D, frequently severely damaged.

sources.title: ASPCA: Rhododendron
sources.note: Toxic to dogs, cats and horses (grayanotoxin); a few leaves can cause serious problems.
